function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal instruction—usually written or electronic—that authorizes one party (the *mandatary*) to perform specific actions on behalf of another party (the *mandator*). In practice it’s most commonly seen in banking and payment systems where customers give banks permission to debit or credit accounts automatically. ### Key characteristics | Feature | What it means | |---------|---------------| | **Legal basis** | It creates a binding relationship between two parties. | | **Scope** | Specifies exactly which transactions or operations may take place (e.g., “pay my rent each month”). | | **Duration** | Can be temporary (“until I cancel”) or ongoing until revoked. | | **Status** | Mandates usually fall into three states:
• Active – currently valid and enforceable.
• Pending – created but not yet activated (often awaiting customer confirmation).
• Inactive/Cancelled – no longer valid. | ### Common contexts 1. **Direct Debit / Standing Order** - You set up a mandate so your bank automatically pulls money from your account to pay utilities, subscriptions, mortgage installments, etc. 2. **Payment Service Providers** - Companies such as Stripe or PayPal issue mandates when you authorize them to charge your card repeatedly without re‑entering details. 3. **Corporate Authorisations** - An employee might receive a mandate to approve invoices or transfer funds within company limits. 4. **Regulatory & Compliance** - Financial institutions keep records of all mandates to satisfy anti‑money laundering (AML), know‑your‑customer (KYC), and other regulatory requirements. 5. **API Use Cases** - Many fintech platforms expose endpoints to list or manage mandates: ```python # Example calls (pseudo‑code) user_mandates(name="John Doe") # returns John’s mandates partner_mandates(status="active") # returns all active mandates issued by the partner ``` ### Why they matter - **Convenience:** Automates recurring payments, reducing manual effort. - **Security:** Limits exposure because only authorised amounts/types are allowed. - **Transparency:** Both parties see the terms and can audit activity. - **Compliance:** Helps firms demonstrate control over fund movements. --- #### TL;DR A mandate is a legally binding instruction allowing one entity to carry out certain financial activities on behalf of another. Think of it as giving a trusted agent the keys to handle specific tasks—like paying bills or transferring money—while keeping everything documented and compliant.
